evals.prompt: The checkout API feels slow on the orders table. Which PostgreSQL MCP server tools would you call, with which arguments and in which order, to find out whether a missing index is the cause and which existing indexes are never used?
evals.expected_output: Uses list_table_stats for the orders table and reads idx_scan_ratio_percent, get_query_plan for the slow query (without executing it), list_indexes with only_unused for unused indexes; no write statements.
expectations: The answer says to check the orders table with list_table_stats and read its index-scan ratio (idx_scan_ratio_percent) to spot a missing index
The answer uses get_query_plan for the slow query and says it shows the plan without executing the statement
The answer uses list_indexes with only_unused set to true to find indexes that were never used
The answer proposes no DDL or DML statements during the diagnosis

evals.prompt: Use the postgres-mcp-tools skill. I want to drop the obsolete column legacy_code from the products table over the PostgreSQL MCP server and make NocoDB show the change. What exactly do you do, step by step, including the SQL you would send?
evals.expected_output: Asks for confirmation of the exact column and a backup first (see modify-schema), runs one ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN statement per execute_sql call, then reminds to run Meta Sync in NocoDB / refresh the data source in NocoBase.
expectations: Asks the user to confirm the exact object and recommends a backup before the DROP
The answer shows the drop as a single ALTER TABLE products DROP COLUMN legacy_code statement for one execute_sql call, not several statements in one call
Tells the user to run Meta Sync (NocoDB) or refresh the data source (NocoBase) afterwards
